page: Amazon Web Services c7i.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at a base clock of 3.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system provides 32 vCPUs distributed across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem is backed by 105 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and hardware support for advanced instruction sets including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), AVX-512, and cryptographic acceleration instructions such as VAES and SHA-NI.

The compute profile is paired with 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, delivering an exact 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per virtual core. The instance includes a 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. There are no dedicated graphics processing units attached (0.0 GPUs), and the instance does not feature local instance storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions for all persistence requirements.

Benchmark evaluations position the c7i.8xlarge within the middle tier across most standard compute metrics, with a PassMark CPU score of 42487.77 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 14186.0. However, specific workloads show distinct advantages. Single-threaded gzip compression performs in the upper 25% at 32.2 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput reaches 48.15 GB/sec, also ranking in the top quartile. In machine learning inference evaluations, the server leverages its vector and matrix extensions to reach top-tier throughput (top 10%) on small LLM text generation at 380.26 tokens per second, alongside strong prompt processing on medium 7B models at 206.92 tokens per second.

With its dense dedicated compute allocation, contemporary DDR5 memory subsystem, and AMX support, the c7i.8xlarge provides balanced compute efficiency without the overhead of unused accelerator silicon or stranded local disk capacity. The configuration is best aligned with continuous integration build environments, computational fluid dynamics, media transcoding, static content distribution, and CPU-driven machine learning inference pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services c7i.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and a 3.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8488C processor. Operating on x86_64 architecture, it delivers 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores paired with 64.0 GB of high-speed 5 GHz DDR5 memory, yielding a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The instance includes 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains no integrated GPU accelerators, and provides no local NVMe storage. Benchmarks demonstrate solid mid-range performance overall, highlighted by strong results in single-threaded gzip compression, static web delivery, and top-tier token throughput in lightweight CPU-based LLM inference via Intel AMX instructions. The c7i.8xlarge is tailored for compute-heavy workloads such as compilation, media processing, high-volume web serving, and CPU inference.
